subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should this Telegram/source-channel false-success class become a core delivery/tool-evidence invariant, or should core stay limited to delivery diagnostics while generic claim verification remains plugin/ClawHub policy?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans agent finalization, Telegram/source-channel delivery, tool evidence, and plugin hook/API scope; choosing fail-closed core behavior versus plugin policy changes product defaults and compatibility.

options.title: Core stays narrow plus plugin seam
options.body: Keep core focused on source-channel delivery invariants and, if needed, close the hook-correlation gap so a claim-verification plugin can enforce this policy outside core.

options.title: Add core claim verification
options.body: Implement a core turn-level side-effect ledger that warns, blocks, or retries unsupported success claims before Telegram/source-channel delivery.

options.title: Force tool-only Telegram DMs
options.body: Make Telegram direct messages require message-tool delivery by default, reducing one false-success path but changing existing direct-chat behavior.

recommendation.title: Core stays narrow plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Keep core focused on source-channel delivery invariants and, if needed, close the hook-correlation gap so a claim-verification plugin can enforce this policy outside core.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged guardrail and the broad claim-verification scope decision both route through this person, making them the best available owner for the product-boundary call.
